**3.11.1a P1's site form — a world site's coherence expectation, its autocorrect and its anomalies** (the owner's word
of 2026-10-18, J393). For a `Placement` whose subject is a site, P1 measures the site against its **kind's coherence
expectation** — the kind row's `roadAccess`, `expect`, `autocorrect` and `autocorrectM` (V14 §2.5), read through the
resolver by kind (R-V14-14), the card's `roadAccess` its own copy — in place of the seven frame terms (a site is
world-first and has no frame to measure). `siteCoherence(world, site, origin)` returns the `CoherenceCost` of the site
terms, each ≥ 0 before its weight, read over the routes of the network in force other than site trails (a hidden road counts
as no public road; V13 §3.8 (9), (12)):

| term | measures | the raw cost |
|---|---|---|
| `siteAccess` | the card's `roadAccess` against the route layer | `on`: 0 when a route's polyline lies within `site.onWithinM` of the origin, else 1; `onRiverCrossing`: 0 when a route's crossing of a reach (the polyline's intersection with a course of `WorldRoute.crossings`) lies within `site.onWithinM`, else 1; `served`: 0 on a standalone world (W7 seats it, V13 §3.8 (1)) and on a host-bound world when a host route lies within the kind's `autocorrectM` (the via re-lay comes, V13 §3.8 (12)), else 1; `reached`: 0 when a routed cell lies within `site.trailMaxM` (the site trail comes), else 1; `none`: 0; `shunned`: 1 when a route lies within `site.shunWithinM`, else 0 |
| `siteExpect` (one row per `expect` entry, its `detail` the entry's terms) | the greatest of the entry's terms — V14's own `SuitabilityTerm` plug-ins, `terms.get(id).compute(cell, ctx)` at the origin's fine cell (V13 §2.2) | max(0, `min` − value) ÷ `min` |

At the edit a `served` or `reached` kind's access reads 0 where the edit itself brings the road (W7 standalone, the
via re-lay host-bound, the site trail); at every later read (the anomalies below) it reads the network as laid — a
route ending at or passing within `site.onWithinM` of the origin, its site trail standing — so a road W7 could not
lay shows as `siteOffRoute`.

`total = Σ w_t · raw_t` at `place.coherence`'s `siteAccess` and `siteExpect` weights; `lawful = total ≤ lawfulMax`, the
one bound. The bearing is not searched: a site's bearing is V14 G3 (a)'s (its approach side facing the nearest route,
else north), re-read after a move. **The autocorrect** runs in the dry run of the edit — a site's `requestCharter` (V14's
`dropSite`) or `setPlacement` — so the DM sees it as the ghost before accepting and nothing moves after: (1) lawful:
placed as asked; (2) unlawful, the kind's `autocorrect` `move`, and a lawful candidate within its `autocorrectM`: **bent**
to the first, named in one line by `bend.site.placement` with the distance and the term it meets ("moved 140 m onto the
road"), the ghost at the bent origin, the bearing re-read — the base's bend (§7.1, item 101 R2); (3) `autocorrect`
`bring`: its `siteAccess` reads 0 wherever the road can come (a standalone world always; a host-bound one within
`autocorrectM`, the via re-lay laid with the edit), so only an unmet expectation or a host route beyond reach leaves it
unlawful, and it is never moved; (4) `autocorrect` `hold` (`autocorrectM` 0): never moved; (5) still unlawful: F-PLACE's
rung "no lawful placement within reach" — the asked origin kept, flagged unlawful, the three least-cost candidates
within `site.siteSearchM` offered as ghosts (`W_PLACE_NO_LAWFUL`: `keep`, the default for a `hold` kind, recorded as
`accept: ['unlawful']` on the event; `takeOffer` with `offer: n`; `cancel`), none beyond (`W_PLACE_NO_LAWFUL` with no
offer). **`nearestLawful(world, site, origin)`** evaluates, in this order, the asked origin; for an `on` or `onRiverCrossing`
kind the nearest point of each route's polyline, or each route–reach crossing, within the reach; then the fine-cell
centres on V13 §3.11.1's spiral at a step of one cell — first out to the kind's `autocorrectM` (the autocorrect's reach),
then to `site.siteSearchM` (the offers') — skipping a water cell and a point inside a placed frame's extent (a free
site never stands inside a frame; V14's J-V14.41); it returns up to three lawful candidates by ascending `total`, ties
by distance from the asked origin, then by cell index, then by route id (V13 §3.7 (6)'s order: no draw). **A
host-placed site** (its `Placement.hostLocked`, the host's record its position; V14 §3.4 (a): never re-sited) runs no
search: its cost is measured and reported, its anomalies carry `keep` alone, and a `served` kind's via re-lay is still
offered (it moves the road, never the site). **The anomalies** `siteOffRoute`, `siteOnRoute` and `siteExpectation`
(V13 §2.2) are a site placement's derived readings of these terms over the world as it stands — read at every
placement edit (P5), on its card, by the `anomalies` layer and by the clerk — so a later route edit, a host network
change, or a cascade that moves a reach or thins a resource shows at the next read and moves nothing;
`Placement.coherenceCost` stays the last edit's (a later edit never re-opens a placement, as politics never does). The
DM's choices are `W_PLACE_ANOMALY`'s — `keep` (default) or `worldWins`, on a site its re-materialization (V14 §3.4
(a)) — or a `setPlacement`, whose dry run corrects and offers again. Every bend, offer and anomaly writes its
`ReasonRecord` (the kind row's cells and `place.coherence`'s, the routes and the term values read, the asked and the
bent origin with the distance), so the clerk's `why placement` answers "moved 140 m onto the road: a toll house stands
on its road". The precedence stamp of a site placement stays `world`; the autocorrect changes no stamp and no arena
(bar 3).
